subject: SLA exception sampler coordination: console routing + guided sampling runbook
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA exception sampler coordination: console routing + guided sampling runbook

Team —

Quick background: ACME reported a recurring SLA exception pattern where high-cost / high-latency routes (mostly long-chat summarize flows) spike briefly and then disappear. Procurement wants predictable billing exposure and a playbook we can hand the customer and their procurement/legal teams.

Ask: can product + console + infra produce a short runbook (2–4 pages) and a minimal console UX flow that: 1) surfaces the active exception (route + percentile), 2) recommends a guided sampling policy (sample rate + fallback model), and 3) offers a one-click canary/fallback or annotated incident link? We need a draft by EOD tomorrow so we can share with ACME in our Friday sync.

Important constraints:
- Must be actionable for Customer Success on-call (no heavy infra ops steps)
- Sampling guidance should include cost delta estimates (token units) and expected tail-latency impact
- Playbook must reference audit/telemetry links and describe how we fall back to lower-capacity variants without losing user experience

I attached a short template and a sampling matrix for reference. If infra/product can sketch an initial console mock and the UX text I will consolidate and take to CS/AM.

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Observability Product
Redwood Inference

Attachments: console-sla-exception-sampler-draft.pdf (template), sampling-routing-matrix.xlsx (matrix)

Thanks for the context — I can take point on the runbook copy and UX language. A couple of clarifying Qs before I start drafting:

1) What do we want the "exception" trigger to be? 95th latency > X ms for Y minutes, or cost-per-minute delta > $Z? I can include both but want a primary SLO.
2) For the guided sampling recommendations: do we prefer to ship a default policy (e.g., linear decrement sample rates by 50%/25%/10%) or propose a per-customer calibrated policy?

If you can confirm those two points I will produce a 1.5 page runbook draft and a companion 2-step console copy you can paste into the UX mock.

— Jasmine
Product Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA exception sampler coordination: console routing + guided sampling runbook

Marcus / Jasmine —

We're on this. Quick infra stance and proposal:

- Trigger: 95th percentile latency > 1.2x baseline for 10 continuous minutes OR token-cost variance > 40% vs baseline for a 5-minute window. That keeps us sensitive to latency regressions and sudden cost spikes from runaway prompts.
- Default sampling policy: fallback ladder of [50%, 25%, 10%] over 3 minutes, with automated KV-prefix-preserving sampling so we keep coherent context for long chats. We will provide estimated cost change numbers for a typical summarize route (see attached matrix).
- Console UX proposal: add a compact "Exception Card" in the route insights page showing: route name, observed window (start/end), metric delta, recommended sampling step, one-click apply (simulated dry-run link), and a link to open a ticket + annotated trace.

Delivery: I can ship a lightweight UI mock (Figma link in the Drive doc) and a first-pass draft of the runbook text by EOD tomorrow. We will need CS to validate wording around what they can and cannot do without infra escalation.

Forwarded attachment: console-sla-exception-sampler-draft.pdf

— Jonas
Principal Reliability Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
